4271.title: Add SKPaint.GetFastBounds() for quick-reject culling
4271.body:
Add SKPaint.GetFastBounds() for quick-reject culling (#4271)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/271
Submodule: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/b16789ec35...280ec21ada

Expose Skia's public SkPaint::computeFastBounds / canComputeFastBounds as a
single Try-style method:

    bool SKPaint.GetFastBounds(SKRect bounds, out SKRect fastBounds)

It returns the conservative device-space rectangle a paint can draw into for a
given source rect, composing the paint's path effect, stroke inflation, mask
filter and image filter. Paired with the already-bound SKCanvas.QuickReject it
completes the quick-reject culling pattern Skia documents in its own headers:

    if (paint.GetFastBounds(path.Bounds, out var fast) && canvas.QuickReject(fast))
        return; // skip the draw

One method instead of a Can* property plus a Compute* method:
Skia's contract is that canComputeFastBounds() is a guard that must be checked
before calling computeFastBounds() - the result is unreliable for paints whose
image filter or path effect cannot report bounds (the header says "Only call
this if canComputeFastBounds() returned true"). Folding that guard into the
bool return makes the API impossible to misuse and matches the existing
out-bool bounds family - SKPath.GetBounds, SKPath.GetTightBounds,
SKCanvas.GetLocalClipBounds - none of which has a paired Can* property (there is
no CanGetTightBounds). GetFastBounds returns false (and SKRect.Empty) when the
paint cannot compute fast bounds.

Public SkPaint API, not SkMaskFilter:
This began as a binding of SkMaskFilter::computeFastBounds, but that method has
been private since 2018 (mono/skia 80747ef591, "move the guts of SkMaskFilter.h
into SkMaskFilterBase.h") and binding it would require the internal
SkMaskFilterBase.h. SkPaint::computeFastBounds is the public entry point, has
stayed public for 8 years despite a "(to be made private)" doc note, and
composes the mask-filter bounds internally, so it is a strict superset of the
per-mask-filter method. SkImageFilter::computeFastBounds likewise stayed public,
reinforcing SkPaint as the intended API. The skia-discuss thread EFbFlfJjNxE
("How to get the path bound including border?") also recommends computeFastBounds
as the way to get a shape's bounds including blur/shadow.

  * C API (mono/skia#271): sk_paint_compute_fast_bounds,
    sk_paint_can_compute_fast_bounds; regenerated SkiaApi.generated.cs.
  * Bump externals/skia b16789ec35 -> 280ec21ada to pick up the C API.
  * Tests (SKPaintTest): blur outset 3x sigma, stroke (round join/cap) outset
    strokeWidth/2, stroke+blur composition, fill no-op returns source, source
    rect not mutated, returns true for simple paints, managed/native parity.
  * Gallery sample PaintFastBoundsSample and PaintFastBoundsBenchmark
    (quick-reject culling vs. unconditional draw).

4258.title: Harden Skia upstream-sync: conflict policy, durable gn args, standalone skill, honest run signal
4258.body:
Harden Skia upstream-sync: conflict policy, durable gn args, standalone skill, honest run signal (#4258)

Follow-up to the mode=main tip work (#4254) and release-line targeting
(#4239). The first real tip runs exposed three rough edges in the
auto-skia-sync automation, plus that key Skia-update knowledge lived only
in the workflow prompt where the update-skia skill couldn't reach it.

~~ Verify-upstream-or-reapply conflict resolution ~~

A tip merge runs ~291 commits ahead of our submodule base and conflicts on
every file carrying an [M1xx] fork cherry-pick. The old "keep ours / resolve
what you reasonably can" guidance risked silently dropping a not-yet-
upstreamed patch (--theirs) or freezing a stale form of one upstream had
since refined (--ours; e.g. our SDF-LCD patch used getMaxScale() while
upstream relanded it as sk_ieee_float_divide(1.f, getMinScale())).

Replace it with an explicit, auditable policy: classify each fork patch on a
conflicted file as upstreamed (take upstream's form, record the SHA) or not
upstreamed (re-apply ours on top) -- never a blanket --theirs/--ours, never
a silent drop. A mandatory before-merge fork-patch snapshot is cross-checked
so every patch lands in the resolution table as upstreamed or re-applied; a
patch that is neither is a lost patch -> stop and fix. Applied across gotcha
#15, SKILL.md Phase 5, and the workflow tip note.

~~ Allow a required new gn arg through build.cake ~~

The tip build needed skia_use_partition_alloc=false because upstream now
defaults it to is_clang while our DEPS deliberately omits partition_alloc;
Skia ships an official zero-overhead noop raw_ptr for exactly this case, so
=false is the supported embedder path, not a hack. The rule banned all
build.cake edits, forcing a one-off --gnArgs CLI flag and leaving durable
config non-durable.

Split the rule into two tiers: still forbid changing compiler/linker flags
(or scripts/infra/native/**) to silence a host build error, but allow adding
a genuinely required new upstream gn arg to the affected platforms'
native/**/build.cake gn-args lists, flagged in both PR summaries for cross-
platform review. Sequencing is honored: the toggle doesn't exist in m150, so
the relaxed rule lets the next milestone merge add it in-context rather than
breaking the current build. Recommendation for the eventual bump (gotcha #23):
keep partition_alloc disabled via the supported noop, not by vendoring the
Chromium allocator.

~~ Make the skill standalone; reduce the workflow to CI overrides ~~

main/tip mode and the required-new-gn-arg rule were documented only in the
workflow prompt, so the update-skia skill couldn't drive them locally. Move
both into the skill: tip mode becomes a first-class third option in Phase 1
(new {UPSTREAM_REF} variable, merge-base..upstream/main milestone diffs,
generalized Phase 5 merge command), and the gn-arg rule lands in Phase 7
backed by gotcha #23. Trim the workflow's duplicated build.cake/mode prose to
short pointers, keeping only genuinely CI-specific guardrails (can't apt-
install in the sandbox; a missing host dep is a workflow bug, not a flag hack;
Linux-only-build cross-platform review). These are prompt-body edits, so the
lock stays byte-identical.

~~ Stop mislabeling a real sync as a no-op ~~

A sync that merged upstream, built, tested, and opened both PRs was reported
by the gh-aw conclusion job as a no-op, which then failed trying to file a
no-op issue (the workflow has no issues: write). Cause: safe-outputs staged
mode blocks the agent from creating anything directly -- the real PRs are
opened by the host post-step skia-sync-push-prs.sh with the autobump token --
so noop was the agent's only completion signal and every run, real or not,
signalled noop.

Give the agent an honest signal: declare create-pull-request in safe-outputs,
kept staged (preview-only; the safe_outputs job is ubuntu-slim with
permissions:{} and never touches the workspace) so a real sync registers as a
pull-request output, while real PRs still come only from the post-step. Set
noop: report-as-issue: false so noop is reserved for genuine no-work runs and
no longer files an uncreatable issue; drop the unused create_issue offer; and
add a "Completion signal" section to the prompt. This is the one frontmatter
edit in the PR, so auto-skia-sync.lock.yml is regenerated.

Validated end-to-end by run 28269474099 (mode=main, real 2-commit merge): the
agent emitted a staged create_pull_request, the conclusion logged no noop with
no failed issue step, and the post-step still pushed skia-sync/main to both
repos and updated the real PRs (#4263 + #269). Rebased on main to pick up the
#4260 workflow rename (lock recompiled to a 0-diff) and confirm consistency
with the #4267 support-status model.

4269.title: Fix small-sigma raster blur regression (define SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS)
4269.body:
Skia's SkBlurEngine refactor (~m129) routes small-sigma blurs of 8888 images
through the raster-pipeline shader-based GaussianPass, which is dramatically
slower than the old dedicated box-approximation path. Chromium mitigates this by
defining SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS (skia/config/SkUserConfig.h), which
makes Raster8888BlurAlgorithm skip GaussianPass and use ThreeBoxApproxPass /
TentPass instead. SkiaSharp never defined it, so the CPU blur path is fully
exposed to the regression.

Define SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS for all libSkiaSharp native builds
(linux covers linuxnodeps; ios covers maccatalyst; plus macos, windows, android,
tvos, wasm, and tizen's project_def.prop).

Measured on a Linux x64 source build, same-milestone A/B (stock m150 vs m150 +
define): small-sigma image blur recovers ~6x (2.84 ms -> 455 us), beating the
3.119 baseline, with no measurable change to any other benchmark. The change is
a pure compile-time define and is build-verified on Linux x64.

4267.title: Group release-notes site by support status (stable/preview) + audit drift check
4267.body:
Group the release-notes site by support status, with an audit drift check (#4267)

Context: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/chrome-release-channels
Spec: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md §3.5

The release-notes site (documentation/docfx/releases/) listed every SkiaSharp
version in one flat list, so neither the sidebar nor the landing page gave any
signal about what is actually supported. A reader had to already know that, say,
4.148 is the stable line and 4.150 is the in-flight preview. This groups the
site by support status and keeps that grouping honest over time.

SkiaSharp ships NuGet packages (not a multi-tier channel product), so support is
modelled as two hand-maintained lists in scripts/infra/docs/versions.json — a
`stable` line for production and a `preview` line for the milestone currently
being stabilized — which correspond to Chrome's Stable/Extended-Stable and Beta
channels. Today that is {stable: ["4.148"], preview: ["4.150"]}: 4.148 sits on
Chrome Extended Stable while 4.150 is the preview about to promote (149 was
skipped), i.e. the promotion gap.

generate-release-notes.py consumes the block to organise both outputs:

- TOC.yml keeps supported lines at top level; 4.147.x and older 3.x fold into an
  "Out of Support Versions" node and 1.x/2.x into "Obsolete Versions".
- index.md opens with a "Support overview" — a stable/preview/out-of-support/
  obsolete lifecycle legend plus a table of the currently-supported lines and
  their latest release — then the detailed per-line lists and the folded
  out-of-support / obsolete sections. An empty/absent block falls back to the
  legacy flat layout, so the feature is purely additive.

The block is curated by hand on purpose: SkiaSharp does not ship every Chrome
milestone, so auto-deriving it from Chromium Dash would point a tier at a
milestone with no release line and could mark the actually-shipped lines as
unsupported. To catch the block going stale instead of silently auto-changing
it, the security audit's milestone heads-up (query-milestone-schedule.py, Step
3) — which already fetches the live Chrome channels — now also compares the
block to them and emits an ok/warn/drift verdict via a new `support` output
section. Drift is a detection-only audit finding; the fix is always a manual
edit of versions.json. The decision table (including the promotion-gap
exception) is documented in the spec, SKILL.md, and references/milestone-
schedule.md, and unit-tested across the full set of channel combinations.

CI-generated TOC.yml/index.md are intentionally not committed here; the
release-notes pipeline regenerates them on main. Verified by dispatching that
pipeline against this branch: the generator ran clean (errors: []) and produced
the groupings above.

4260.title: ci: regroup and rename GitHub Actions workflows; prune dead ones
4260.body:
[CI] Regroup and rename GitHub Actions workflows; prune dead ones (#4260)

The Actions sidebar sorts alphabetically by workflow `name`, so shared
prefixes are the only thing that visually groups related workflows. Only
the `Docs - *` set was grouped; everything else was scattered. This PR
renames workflows into three intent-based groups, removes long-disabled
superseded ones, and fixes every place that references a workflow by name.

Groups:

  * Pages - * (was Docs - *; this is the GitHub Pages/site infra, not API
    docs): Deploy, Go Live!, PR Staging - Cleanup, PR Staging - Sweep Stale
  * PR - * (event-driven PR helpers): Backport, Rebase, Artifacts Comment
  * Sync - * (scheduled commit-back / sync bots): Skia Upstream, Docs
    Submodule, Release Notes & API Diffs, Agentic Data, Issue Triage, Samples

`Manage NuGet Feed` and `Copilot Setup Steps` stay standalone (the latter
keeps its exact name — GitHub special-cases it).

Renaming a workflow is not just the `name:` line: `workflow_run` triggers
and our tooling reference workflows *by name*, so those references are
updated in lockstep to avoid silently breaking the chained automation:

  * build-site-go-live.yml `workflow_run` -> Pages names
  * persist-aw-data.yml `workflow_run` trigger *and* its `resolve_key`
    case -> `Sync - Issue Triage`
  * recompiled the three gh-aw `*.lock.yml` files from their `.md` sources
    via `gh aw compile` (name-only diffs; never hand-edited)
  * .agents/skills/ci-status/* (dashboard `GITHUB_WORKFLOWS` map, tables,
    severity lists, sample output) and release-publish/SKILL.md, which call
    `gh workflow run` by name
  * documentation/dev/writing-docs.md and maintaining.md prose

Removed four superseded, already-disabled workflows — issue triage and
labeling are now handled by the agentic `Sync - Issue Triage`:

  * similarissues.yml, label-with-ai.yml, triage-and-repro.yml,
    engagement-scores.yml

Historical entries under documentation/docfx/releases/* are left unchanged
on purpose — they record past PR titles and are an immutable changelog.

Note: several "ghost" workflows (deleted files whose run history kept them
in the UI) were cleared separately by deleting their run history, since
GitHub has no delete button for a fileless workflow.

4247.title: perf(SKSurface): cache the Canvas wrapper across calls
4247.body:
Cache the SKSurface.Canvas wrapper across calls (#4247)

SKSurface.Canvas did real work on every access: a P/Invoke
(sk_surface_get_canvas), a locked HandleDictionary lookup (a
ReaderWriterLockSlim upgradeable-read lock), and an OwnedBy
ConcurrentDictionary registration. Draw-heavy render loops that fetch the
canvas once per draw call hammer that path, making the getter a measurable
bottleneck.

Cache the managed SKCanvas wrapper on the surface and reuse it, re-fetching
only when the cached wrapper was disposed out from under us; drop the cache
in DisposeManaged. Per-getter cost drops from ~31 ns to ~0.67 ns (a field
read + handle check) with zero allocations, so fetching Canvas per draw now
matches hand-caching it.

This is safe because Skia returns a stable SkCanvas* for the surface's
lifetime. sk_surface_get_canvas forwards to SkSurface::getCanvas(), which
delegates to SkSurface_Base::getCachedCanvas(); that method lazily creates
the canvas once and only ever assigns fCachedCanvas inside its null-guard --
it is never reset or reassigned. The guarantee lives in the shared base, so
it holds for all backends (raster, Ganesh, Graphite, null), and copy-on-write
forks the device's backing store without recreating the SkCanvas, so the
pointer is unaffected.

The one wrinkle is the anti-pattern of explicitly disposing the
surface-owned canvas. That wrapper is created with owns:false, so disposing
it does not call sk_canvas_destroy (the native canvas survives) and it
deregisters itself by identity from HandleDictionary. The
canvas.Handle == IntPtr.Zero guard detects this and re-fetches a fresh,
usable wrapper around the still-alive native canvas.

Notes:
  - No public API changes; adds a private field and a protected override.
    ABI-safe.
  - The cache field is now read/written without the HandleDictionary lock the
    old path incidentally took. Benign under SkiaSharp's single-thread-per-
    surface model (a concurrent race resolves to the same instance).

Tests: SKSurfaceTest gains CanvasReturnsSameInstanceAcrossCalls (regression
guard) and CanvasIsRefetchedAfterExplicitCanvasDispose (covers the new
re-fetch path). Adds SurfaceCanvasBenchmark simulating a 1,000-draw/frame
render loop; Program.cs switches to BenchmarkSwitcher so individual
benchmarks can be selected via args.

4254.title: Add a main (tip) mode to the Skia upstream sync
4254.body:
Add a main (tip) mode to the Skia upstream sync (#4254)

The auto-skia-sync workflow could only track chrome/m<N> milestone
branches (current/next/latest). There was no way to sync against the
in-development tip of upstream Skia, so we couldn't smoke-test bleeding-
edge API/binding changes ahead of a milestone branch cut.

Add a dispatch-only `main` mode that merges google/skia `main` HEAD into
SkiaSharp `main` / mono/skia `skiasharp`. It is explicitly NOT a version
bump: the target milestone stays equal to main's current milestone (no
soname/nuget/milestone changes), and it uses a distinct head branch so a
tip sync never collides with the `current` milestone sync branch.

Changes:

  * skia-sync-detect.sh: introduce an UPSTREAM_REF concept (the google/skia
    ref we merge *from*) so the gate and prompt aren't hardcoded to
    chrome/m<TARGET>. `mode=main` resolves UPSTREAM_REF=main,
    TARGET=MAIN_MS, HEAD_BRANCH=skia-sync/main; all other modes keep
    chrome/m<TARGET> + skia-sync/m<TARGET>. Release detection stays skipped
    for main (TARGET == MAIN_MS), so current == target. Emit a new
    upstream_ref output and gate on ${UPSTREAM_REF}.
  * auto-skia-sync.md: add `main` to the workflow_dispatch mode options,
    surface upstream_ref as a pre-activation output / in the prompt header /
    in the skia-sync-env.sh heredoc, fetch the resolved upstream ref in
    Phase 1 instead of a hardcoded chrome/m<target>, and document the
    tip/bleeding-edge semantics. Lock recompiled (model + native build setup
    unchanged).
  * skia-sync-push-prs.sh: make PR titles/bodies UPSTREAM_REF-aware
    ("Merge upstream Skia main (tip)" vs the milestone titles), defaulting
    to chrome/m<TARGET> when unset for backward compat.

Validation: `gh aw compile` = 0 errors (claude-opus-4.7 preserved);
shellcheck --severity=style clean on all three scripts; a stubbed detect
smoke test confirms current/next/latest/main/default/--milestone N/empty-
milestone resolve correctly and that mode=main yields upstream_ref=main,
head_branch=skia-sync/main, target == current == main's milestone.

A real dispatched run of the new path (actions/runs/28208236195) gated
PROCEED, merged the main tip (~291 commits, 7 conflicts all resolved),
built and tested green on Linux x64 (5569 passed / 0 failed), and opened
the expected draft PRs mono/SkiaSharp#4255 and mono/skia#267.

4239.title: Support release-branch targeting in Skia upstream sync (+ Opus 4.7, libc++ build fix)
4239.body:
Support release-branch targeting in Skia upstream sync (#4239)

The daily Skia upstream sync (`auto-skia-sync`) could only ever target
`main`/`skiasharp`. Maintenance lines such as `release/4.148.x` still need
ongoing bug-fix syncs from upstream Skia, and there was no way to drive one.
This teaches the workflow to sync a `release/{major}.{milestone}.x` line and
open PRs against it in both mono/SkiaSharp and mono/skia, while keeping the
existing `main` behavior unchanged.

~~ Release-line targeting ~~

`skia-sync-detect.sh` becomes the single source of truth for milestone/branch
resolution. It derives the target milestone from the trigger (cron
current/next/latest, or an explicit `milestone` dispatch input) and only looks
for a release line when the target is numerically older than main's milestone
(the newest line is always served by `main`). A maintenance line shares the
same branch name in both repos (`release/{major}.{milestone}.x`). It fails fast
when the matching mono/skia release branch is missing — those branches are
owned by the separate release process, not this sync — and hard-fails rather
than guessing when a milestone matches multiple release branches.
`skia-sync-align-submodule.sh` points `externals/skia` at the SHA the base
branch records before the agent runs, since the agent checks out the workflow
branch (usually `main`) rather than the target line.

~~ Extract detection into committed scripts ~~

The milestone/branch logic previously lived as two large, duplicated inline
bash blocks in the workflow YAML. It is now extracted into committed,
shellcheck-clean scripts, collapsing the `run:` blocks to ~1 and ~5 lines. The
`pre_activation` gate runs the detector (`--gate`) and writes job outputs; the
agent's align step re-runs the same detector without `--gate` and sources its
output, because the agent job only `needs: activation` and cannot read
`pre_activation`'s outputs in gh-aw. The extraction also folds in two review
fixes: numeric `-lt` comparison (was `!=`) and a hard-fail on multi-match (was
a silent `head -1`).

~~ Resolve mode from cron in the workflow ~~

The cron→mode mapping (7 AM → current, 5 PM → latest, else → next) was the only
workflow-coupled knowledge left in the detector — it hardcoded the literal cron
strings and read INPUT_MODE/INPUT_MILESTONE/SCHEDULE env vars. That mapping now
lives in the workflow as a single GitHub Actions expression, next to where the
crons are declared, and the detector takes real `--mode`/`--milestone`
arguments. The script no longer knows anything about cron, so it is
self-contained and unit-testable (`--mode latest` instead of faking
`SCHEDULE='0 17 * * *'`). `mode` is staged into an env var rather than
interpolated straight into `run:`, so the free-form `milestone` dispatch input
cannot inject shell.

~~ Run the agent on Claude Opus 4.7 ~~

The engine is pinned to `claude-opus-4.7` (was the gh-aw default Sonnet). On
this multi-repo, submodule-heavy task Opus produced materially cleaner runs —
no failed commands, retries, or self-introduced build hacks. Opus 4.6 and 4.7
share the same credit multiplier, so this is a free upgrade to the latest
snapshot.

~~ Fix the Linux native build (libc++) ~~

The sync's native build started failing because #4062 ("Migrate Linux Docker
builds to .NET official cross-compilation images") moved the Linux build into
the `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs` cross images, which ship
Clang + libc++. `native/linux/build.cake` now hardcodes `-stdlib=libc++` in
its `extra_cflags`/`extra_ldflags`. The sync builds on a bare `ubuntu-latest`
host — not inside that image — so libc++ was absent and `dotnet cake
--target=externals-linux` failed to link. The agent could not self-remediate:
there is no apt/sudo inside the AWF chroot and the firewall blocks OS package
mirrors, so it got stuck trying to install it. The pre-agent "Install native
build dependencies" step now installs `libc++-dev libc++abi-dev` on the host
(visible to the chroot via the shared filesystem). The agent prompt is also
hardened to forbid patching native build files or compiler/linker flags and
attempting package installs; a genuinely missing host dependency must STOP and
be reported for a human rather than worked around.

Validated end-to-end against `release/4.148.x` with real upstream, native
build, and tests: the skip, idempotent-rerun, and missing-upstream paths behave
correctly, and a full sync produced a clean ~15 min native build with no
build.cake hacks, 5544 tests passing (0 fail / 172 skip), and bug-fix-only PRs
(cgmanifest hash + submodule pointer) on `release/4.148.x` in both repos. The
detector arg interface and all three scripts were re-verified with stubs and
shellcheck. The `release-branch` skill changes are intentionally out of scope
and land separately.

4227.title: Add SKColorFilter.CreateOverdraw() for overdraw visualization
4227.body:
Add SKColorFilter.CreateOverdraw() for overdraw visualization (#4227)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3941
Changes: mono/skia#262

Implements overdraw visualization support by wrapping Skia's
SkOverdrawColorFilter, which maps overdraw counts (0–5+) to a
6-color heat-map palette for rendering performance debugging.

~~ Problem ~~

SkiaSharp wrapped SKOverdrawCanvas (which tracks draw counts by writing
to the alpha channel) but did not expose SkOverdrawColorFilter (which
converts those alpha values into visible colors). Users could generate
overdraw data but not visualize it without dropping into native code.

Issue #3941 requested the missing API to complete the overdraw debugging
workflow.

~~ Solution ~~

Added SKColorFilter.CreateOverdraw() with the standard Span-triple pattern:
  - CreateOverdraw(ReadOnlySpan<SKColor>) — primary overload
  - CreateOverdraw(SKColor[]) — convenience overload

Input validation ensures exactly 6 colors are provided (throws
ArgumentException otherwise, ArgumentNullException for null arrays).

~~ C API ~~

Requires mono/skia#262, which adds sk_colorfilter_new_overdraw() wrapping
SkOverdrawColorFilter::MakeWithSkColors(). The C API accepts a 6-element
color array and returns an sk_colorfilter_t*.

~~ Gallery Sample and Tests ~~

Added OverdrawVisualizationSample showing side-by-side comparison of normal
rendering vs overdraw visualization. The sample demonstrates the full workflow:
  1. Create offscreen A8 surface
  2. Wrap in SKOverdrawCanvas (writes counts to alpha)
  3. Draw overlapping shapes
  4. Snapshot to image
  5. Apply CreateOverdraw filter when drawing the image

Tests cover creation, validation (wrong length, null), Span equivalence,
and rendering with SKOverdrawCanvas to verify the filter correctly maps
alpha values to colors.

~~ Submodule Update ~~

Updates externals/skia to a10e10524a (dev/issue-3941-colorfilter-overdraw
rebased on 214e2d2f38) to include the required C API. The cgmanifest.json
is updated accordingly.

4244.title: Fix integration test harness Docker detection + command timeout, and release-testing skill filter syntax
4244.body:
[Tests] Fix integration harness Docker detection + command timeouts, and release-testing filter syntax (#4244)

Context: found during 4.150.0-preview.2 release testing
Context: Microsoft.Testing.Platform migration #4143

Three latent reliability bugs in the SkiaSharp.Tests.Integration harness
(and the release-testing skill) caused the Linux/Docker test to be silently
skipped, made command timeouts non-functional, and left the release skill
running every test instead of the one requested.

~~ LinuxConsoleTests.IsDockerAvailable() deadlock ~~

The probe set RedirectStandardOutput/Error = true but never drained the
pipes before WaitForExit(10000). `docker info` can emit well over the 64KB
OS pipe buffer, so the child blocked on write while the parent's 10s wait
expired; the subsequent ExitCode read then reported Docker as unavailable
even when the daemon was running. Net effect: the Linux container tests were
ALWAYS skipped.

Drain stdout/stderr via ReadToEndAsync() before WaitForExit, kill the child
on timeout, then Task.WaitAll the reads so a large payload can no longer
deadlock the probe. Verified live: the Linux tests went from Skipped to
actually executing once a real daemon was present.

~~ PlatformTestBase.Run() timeout never enforced ~~

Run() awaited StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()/StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
BEFORE WaitForExit(timeoutSeconds * 1000). ReadToEndAsync only completes when
the stream closes (process exit), so the await blocked until the process
finished and the timeout was effectively dead code — a hung `docker build`
ran unbounded. Reading stdout fully before starting stderr could itself
deadlock if stderr filled.

Start both pipe reads first, enforce the timeout via WaitForExit while the
reads are in flight (Kill(true) on expiry), then await the drained output.
Verified live: SkiaSharpRunsOnLinux passed end-to-end driving a long
`docker build`/`run`, and a cold-cache build correctly threw
TimeoutException after 180s — the exact behavior that was previously
impossible to reach.

~~ release-testing skill uses stale VSTest --filter syntax ~~

After the xUnit v2 -> v3 / Microsoft.Testing.Platform migration (#4143),
VSTest-style `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~X"` is silently
ignored under MTP and runs ALL tests. The skill still documented that form.

Update every command to the MTP form — filter args after the `--` separator
using --filter-class / --filter-method / --filter-namespace with `*`
wildcards — keeping MSBuild -p: properties (SkiaSharpVersion, iOSDevice,
AndroidDeviceId, etc.) BEFORE the separator. Added a note explaining the MTP
requirement so the legacy syntax is not reintroduced.

Verified against the latest published packages (SkiaSharp 4.150.0-preview.2.1
/ HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1-preview.2.1): SmokeTests, ConsoleTests, and both
LinuxConsoleTests pass, and --filter-class/--filter-method correctly narrow
the run under MTP.

4229.title: Add SKImageFilter.CreateCrop()
4229.body:
Add SKImageFilter.CreateCrop() (#4229)

Closes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3938
Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/261

Exposes SkImageFilters::Crop as SKImageFilter.CreateCrop(), the modern
replacement for the deprecated per-filter `cropRect` pattern. Crop restricts
an image filter's output to a rectangle using a tile mode, and composes with
other filters (e.g. blur then crop) instead of every filter carrying its own
crop argument.

Add three ABI-safe overloads (no default parameters):

  * CreateCrop(SKRect)                                  - defaults to Decal
  * CreateCrop(SKRect, SKShaderTileMode)                - null input (source)
  * CreateCrop(SKRect, SKShaderTileMode, SKImageFilter?) - full control

The full overload calls sk_imagefilter_new_crop and uses GC.KeepAlive on the
input filter to keep it alive across the native call. A null input maps to
IntPtr.Zero, which Skia interprets as the source image.

  * binding/SkiaSharp/SKImageFilter.cs       - the three CreateCrop overloads
  * binding/SkiaSharp/SkiaApi.generated.cs   - regenerated P/Invoke binding
  * externals/skia                           - bump to pick up mono/skia#261

Tests in SKImageFilterTest.cs go beyond non-null checks and verify behavior:
null input is accepted, Crop composes with CreateBlur, Decal leaves pixels
outside the crop transparent while Clamp produces a different (edge-extended)
result, and a rendering test confirms pixels inside the rect are drawn and
those outside are cropped away.

ImageFilterCropSample.cs adds an interactive gallery demo with crop bounds
sliders, a tile-mode picker, an "Enable Crop" toggle, and an optional blur
composition, drawing the crop rect as an overlay so the effect is visible.

4228.body:
Add SKImageFilter.CreateEmpty() (#4228)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3937
Changes: depends on mono/skia#260 (sk_imagefilter_new_empty C API)

Skia's SkImageFilters::Empty() produces a transparent-black image filter
that discards its input — useful as an explicit "no content" node in
filter-composition chains and for exercising transparent-black handling.
It was unreachable from managed code because neither the C shim nor the
binding exposed it.

new sk_imagefilter_new_empty() entry point, matching the existing

a ref-counted SKImageFilter the caller owns). The submodule is bumped to
pick up the C API from mono/skia#260, and SkiaApi.generated.cs is
regenerated rather than hand-edited.

  * CreateEmpty returns non-null and a new instance per call (not a
    singleton — distinct handles)
  * the filter composes as both the outer and inner node of
    CreateCompose
  * CreateEmptyDiscardsDrawnContent renders through a shared local
    function so the only variable is the filter: drawing a red rect on
    an explicit blue background yields red with no filter, and yields
    blue with Empty() — proving the filter discards the draw to
    transparent black. Clearing to blue keeps the assertion independent
    of surface zero-initialization.

This direct-draw behavior matches upstream usage in
gm/imagefiltersbase.cpp, which applies Empty() straight to draw ops, and
the transparent-black semantics asserted here mirror

4225.title: docs: drop obsolete GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo page to fix xref collision
4225.body:
The mdoc docs pipeline emits a doc page for both public Vulkan Ycbcr
conversion types, which differ only by the case of a single letter:

  - GRVkYcbcrConversionInfo - the modern struct (the real type)
  - GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo - a soft [Obsolete] forwarder whose only
    members are the two implicit conversion operators to/from the
    modern type ("Use GRVkYcbcrConversionInfo instead.")

mdoc keeps soft-obsolete types, so it produces two ECMA-XML files whose
names differ only by case (SkiaSharp/GRVkYcbcrConversionInfo.xml and
SkiaSharp/GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo.xml). On the Learn/OpenPublishing
publish build's case-insensitive filesystem those two files collide -
one shadows the other - so every cref to the shadowed type fails with
"Cross reference not found". This is the only case-only-colliding public
type pair in the entire API.

Because the legacy type merely forwards to the modern one, the fix is to
stop emitting its page so only the modern type is published and its xref
always resolves. This mirrors the existing SkiaSharp.Views.Android.Resource
special-case in the same docs-format-docs task, removing the obsolete type
from the Type file (DeleteFile), the Overview/index.xml entry, and the
Framework/FrameworksIndex entry using case-sensitive (ordinal) matching so
the modern GR... entry is preserved.

This is the durable companion to mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs PR #152, which
removes the already-committed page manually; this change prevents mdoc
from regenerating it on the next Auto API Docs Writer run.

4221.title: Fix integration test harness for .NET 10
4221.body:
Fix integration test harness for .NET 10 (#4221)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4221

While running the release-testing matrix for 4.148.0, the integration test
harness failed before SkiaSharp was ever exercised: several pieces of the
throwaway-project generators were still pinned to (or rolling forward past)
the wrong SDK/framework, so the temp projects never built.

Two distinct failure modes were in play. The Docker-based Linux console test
still used the .NET 8 SDK image and could not build the net10.0 project
(NETSDK1045). Separately, the temp global.json requested 8.0.0 with
rollForward=latestMajor, which on machines with .NET 11 previews installed
rolled the SDK forward to net11.0 — and `dotnet new maui` then emitted
net11.0-* TFMs that didn't match the net10.0-* frameworks the harness builds
(NETSDK1005, "doesn't have a target for net10.0-*").

Pin every part of the harness to the .NET 10 band:

  * LinuxConsoleTests: bump the Docker base image
    mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 -> sdk:10.0 so the container can build
    the net10.0 temp project.
  * PlatformTestBase: pin the temp global.json to the 10.0.100 SDK band with
    rollForward=latestFeature and allowPrerelease=false, so it stays on 10.0.x
    and never rolls forward to a prerelease major.
  * Pin the template framework explicitly on every `dotnet new` call rather
    than relying on the SDK pin alone. The SDK-bundled console/blazor templates
    do honor the global.json band, but the MAUI workload template defaults to
    the newest installed framework (e.g. net11.0) even when the SDK is pinned,
    so it must be told `-f net10.0`. A shared `BaseFramework` constant in
    PlatformTestBase is now passed via `-f` to the console, blazorwasm, and
    maui generators, keeping all generated TFMs on net10.0 regardless of which
    SDKs/workloads are installed locally.

Validated by running the full integration matrix against the 4.148.0 release
packages (SmokeTests, ConsoleTests, LinuxConsoleTests on sdk:10.0, BlazorTests,
MauiMacCatalyst, MauiiOS on iOS 16.2 + 26.3, MauiAndroid on API 23 + 36) — all
green. (A machine-specific ValidateXcodeVersion=false override was used during
local testing only and is intentionally not part of this change.)

4207.title: [docs] Release-notes: main-only daily workflow + GitHub Release teaser playbook
4207.body:
[docs] Release-notes: main-only daily workflow + GitHub Release teaser playbook (#4207)

Two related changes to how SkiaSharp release notes are produced — one for the
website release-notes/API-diff automation, one for the GitHub Release body.
Skill, workflow, and docs only; no product code.

~~ Harden the website release-notes workflow ~~

The unified "Update Release Notes & API Diffs" workflow was opening duplicate
PRs and occasionally diffing months of history. Two root causes:

  * The agent created a branch but never committed, so gh-aw's patch fallback
    diffed the whole branch (the original E003 failure). It now commits on the
    agent branch *before* gh-aw opens the PR.
  * `release/*` and `v*` tag triggers ran a *stale per-branch copy* of the
    workflow: a push/tag event runs the file living on that ref, not on main.
    That produced the duplicate dev/release-notes-* PRs (#4172, #4208, #4210,
    #4213) alongside the unified bot/release-notes PR.

The Prepare generators already walk every release/* ref and read v* tags
themselves, so one run from main covers all branches. Drop the release/** and
v* triggers, keep push:[main] + workflow_dispatch, and move the safety-net cron
from weekly to daily. Prepare now does `git fetch --tags --force` so a freshly
pushed stable tag flips that version's page to stable on the next run, and it
emits a has_changes flag that gates the agent job — an unchanged daily run
skips the agent and the PR deterministically instead of trusting the LLM to
notice an empty work list.

Because tags no longer auto-trigger, the release-publish skill gains a post-tag
"Refresh Website Release Notes & API Diffs" step (Step 5) that dispatches the
workflow from main so the site updates immediately after a stable release
rather than waiting up to a day for the cron.

~~ GitHub Release teaser playbook ~~

Maintainers found the flat 100+ line auto-generated PR list "too heavy and hard
to find things." Replace the old per-PR emoji-annotation step with a short,
scannable customer teaser, with GitHub's full PR list folded beneath it
(release-publish Step 7). Rename references/release-notes.md to
references/github-release-teaser.md and rewrite it as a self-contained playbook:

  * Classify breaking-first: ⚠️ Breaking → ✨ What's New → 🐛 Fixes →
    📦 Dependency Updates (empty sections omitted). Breaking leads because that
    is what consumers most need to see. The new 🐛 Fixes section surfaces
    consumer-visible bug fixes the old prompt was folding — confirmed by an A/B
    test where two models both missed the same PRs.
  * Treat the Skia milestone bump as a headline ✨ feature, not a dependency;
    routine [skia-sync] engine merges stay folded.
  * Never advertise security: native-library bumps read neutrally as
    "Updated <dep> to <version>"; upstream CVE text stays verbatim only in the
    fold.
  * Credit every contributor inline (by @author (#NNNN)) plus a roll-up of the
    unique community handles.
  * Use a 2-line header: a neutral subtitle, then NuGet · Release notes · Full
    changelog, where the notes link uses the base X.Y.Z line and the compare URL
    moves up out of the fold so it appears once.

The doc is the single source of truth (full rules + a worked example); SKILL.md
Step 7 keeps only a short prompt that defers to it, and Step 5 is trimmed of
generator implementation detail so the runbook stays instruction-focused.

Validated by re-applying the playbook — via agents, reading only each release's
raw auto-generated log — to all six live GitHub Releases (v3.119.4 through
v4.150.0-preview.1.1) and grading each result against the hard rules.

Follow-up: the stale per-version workflow files still living on release/4.148.x
are removed in #4217.

4218.title: [api-docs] Stop merge from writing unfilled remarks scaffold to XML
4218.body:
[api-docs] Don't write unfilled remarks scaffold back to the docs XML (#4218)

Context: #4204 (introduced the extract-time remarks scaffold)

The api-docs writer seeds each type's <remarks> with a markdown scaffold
("[Describe what this type does ...]") at extract time so the agent has a
structure to complete. The merge step, however, wrote back any field that
was not the literal "To be added." stub — so when a type was only partially
written, the raw scaffold landed in the published XML instead of real prose.

This surfaced in the Auto API Docs Writer run for SKPathBuilder (~200
fields): the agent ran out of time, and SKPathBuilder.xml came back as

    -    <remarks>To be added.</remarks>
    +    <remarks>...[Describe what this type does and when to use it]...

which is worse than the placeholder it replaced. The next run's extractor
only re-collects fields equal to "To be added.", so a scaffolded <remarks>
is never re-detected and the template noise would become permanent.

Centralise placeholder detection in a single Test-IsUnfilled helper shared
by extract and merge, treating both "To be added." and the unfilled scaffold
sentinels as unwritten:

  - merge refuses to write unfilled scaffold, leaving "To be added." intact
    so the XML stays clean and the next run can re-fill it
  - extract now re-collects already-leaked scaffold, so any pollution from
    earlier runs self-heals on the next pass
  - genuine prose is untouched — only the exact scaffold sentinels match, so
    real content containing brackets ([SKPath](...), list[0]) merges normally
  - the remarks template is defined once as $script:TypeRemarksTemplate so
    extract (which injects it) and the detector cannot drift apart

Round-tripped against synthetic stubs for the bug scenario, the self-heal
case, and the bracketed-content false-positive guard, plus the normal
fully-filled path. +35/-7 in docs-tool.ps1 with a matching safety-check
bullet in SKILL.md.

4211.title: Fix release-branch skill integration-branch model and add bump-version helper
4211.body:
Fix release-branch skill integration-branch model and add bump-version helper (#4211)

The release-branch skill carried an incorrect mental model: it treated `main`
as the sole "integration branch" and described stable releases as being cut
from a preview branch. That misrepresents how SkiaSharp actually releases, so
anyone following the skill would target the wrong base branch and bump the
wrong thing.

Correct the model: each release line has its own integration branch — `main`
for the newest in-development line, `release/X.Y.x` for each maintenance line
(e.g. release/3.119.x @ 3.119.5, release/4.148.x @ 4.148.0) — and every release
(preview, rc, stable, patch) is cut from that line's integration branch.

Also fix the bump timing, which is the subtle part. The integration branch must
advance to the next version *immediately when a stable branch is cut* (in
parallel with CI), not after the release publishes: once `release/{version}` is
branched off, PRs keep merging into the integration branch and must land on the
next version, while fixes for the cut release go onto its own `release/{version}`
branch. Leaving the bump until publish lets post-branch merges collide with the
just-released version.

Add scripts/bump-version.ps1 to perform the maintenance-line patch bump safely.
It sets PREVIEW_LABEL and/or bumps the SkiaSharp + HarfBuzzSharp file/nuget
versions in VERSIONS.txt and azure-templates-variables.yml behind a verification
gate, and is deliberately narrow:

  * never touches the assembly versions (pinned at X.Y.0.0 / 1.0.0.0 across
    patches — proven by release/3.119.x sitting at nuget 3.119.5 / assembly
    3.119.0.0)
  * refuses a major.minor change: that is a Skia milestone update (4e08384cd2
    "[skia-sync] Update Skia to milestone m150" also rewrote the milestone/
    soname/increment lines, assembly, cgmanifest.json and native sources), out
    of scope for a version-number helper
  * refuses an equal or lower patch, so a re-run or typo can't publish a
    duplicate/downgraded package
  * fails closed if it cannot parse its guard lines, rather than silently
    skipping the milestone guard
  * requires the caller to supply the HarfBuzzSharp version explicitly; the next
    value increments/appends the 4th digit in lockstep with the SkiaSharp patch
    (14.2.0 -> 14.2.0.1), resetting to 3-digit only on a real native upgrade

Sync documentation/dev/releasing.md (version-pattern and base-branch tables, plus
the Stage 1 flow diagram) to the same model. The helper output was validated
against the real version files for every scenario and independently re-checked by
a code-review pass that ran it dry and live; #4212 (the 4.148.1 bump) is its first
real use. Skill/docs/script only — no C# or native code touched.

4204.title: Improve api-docs skill to stop recurring documentation-writer mistakes
4204.body:
Improve api-docs skill to stop recurring documentation-writer mistakes (#4204)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs/pull/143
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs/pull/148

Reviewing two auto-generated documentation runs against the actual C#
source turned up the same classes of mistakes from the api-docs skill's
writer agent. The root cause was consistent: the writer guessed at facts
it actually had access to. Rather than add more "be careful" prose, this
surfaces those facts as data and teaches the writer and reviewer agents
to verify against source.

~~ Facts the extract tool now provides (scripts/docs-tool.ps1) ~~

  * obsolete: members marked [Obsolete(...)] now carry their attribute,
    with the error flag preserved, so the writer never puts a
    non-compiling API (chiefly legacy SKPaint text rendering) in an
    example and knows the suggested replacement.
  * type-level signature: "public readonly struct ..." vs
    "public class ...", so constructor summaries pick "class" vs "struct"
    and the right "Initializes a new instance of the ..." phrasing.

  These are emitted as top-level entry keys alongside `fields`, so the
  merge step and its _extractedKeys guard are unaffected — verified with
  a synthetic extract -> fill -> merge round-trip (CDATA preserved,
  agent-added fields rejected, signature counts unchanged).

~~ Mistakes from PR #143 ~~

  * CDATA xrefs used a DocId prefix (<xref:T:SkiaSharp.SKPath>), which
    breaks the link; inside CDATA the xref is a bare UID.
  * { get; set; } properties documented as "Gets" instead of
    "Gets or sets" (e.g. SKFontVariationAxis).
  * Constructor summaries dropped the standard
    "Initializes a new instance of the ... class/struct" phrasing.

~~ Mistakes from PR #148 ~~

  * Boolean property <value> used parameter wording ("true to...")
    instead of state wording ("true if...").
  * Struct defaults invented from "typical" constants:
    SKDocumentXpsOptions.Dpi documented as "default 72" when the struct
    zero-inits to 0 (72 is SKDocument.DefaultRasterDpi, used only by the
    scalar CreateXps overloads).
  * Standard-based enums mislabeled: SmpteRp4312 written as RP 432-2
    (it is RP 431-2); SmpteSt4281 (ST 428-1) called "linear" when it is
    a gamma-2.6 transfer. The member name encodes the standard, so the
    skill now cross-checks both the number and the described behavior.
    A Sonnet 4.6 review caught that SmpteSt4281 lives in *both* CICP
    enums (XYZ primaries vs the transfer function), so the guidance is
    split per enum.
  * Examples that don't compile: an undeclared identifier (bitmap2), and
    disposing parent-owned objects (the canvas from SKDocument.BeginPage
    and SKSurface.Canvas are owns:false).

The writer prompt, all three reviewer prompts, the checklist, and the
patterns references are updated together so a fact is taught, verified,
and graded in one place. No product code or generated files change; this
is skill and docs-tooling only.

4200.title: Make doc generation reproducible and Linux-only; unify "API diff" terminology
4200.body:
Make doc generation reproducible and Linux-only; unify "API diff" terminology (#4200)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4200
Companion: mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs#147 (must merge after this)
Supersedes the drifted releases/ baseline committed in #4184.

The repo generates its release documentation through three independent paths,
and two of them produced different output depending on the build host or the
local NuGet-cache warmth. That non-determinism made the doc-bot's regenerated
output "wobble" between runs and was nearly impossible to reproduce locally,
so a reviewer could never tell an intended doc change from host noise. This
PR makes all three paths deterministic, gives them one shared set of entry
points that behave identically locally / in CI / in Docker (Linux), unifies
the "changelog" vs "release notes" terminology onto "API diff", and commits a
freshly regenerated, byte-reproducible baseline.

~~ Path 1 — API diffs: deterministic and correct ~~

Self-dependency resolution used a filesystem glob over the warm package cache,
so the chosen baseline depended on what happened to be unpacked locally. Simply
deleting the glob restored determinism but regressed correctness: ApiInfo must
resolve SkiaSharp.dll to see that the two infrastructure interfaces SKObject
implements (ISKReferenceCounted, ISKSkipObjectRegistration) are internal and
collapse to the public System.IDisposable; without it those internal names
leaked into the public diff (8 files). The fix stages each self-dependency
per-diff at the exact version pinned in that package's own .nuspec
(StageSelfDepsFromNuspecAsync) — contemporaneous, host- and cache-independent.
Two more leaks are closed at the source: auto-generated resource designers
(Android aapt R.*, Uno/WinUI GlobalStaticResources) are excluded via
IgnoreMemberRegex, and the TFM selector now ranks candidates (newest plain
.NET → netstandard → portable) instead of taking filesystem-enumeration order,
so SkiaSharp is diffed from net10.0 and the choice is stable.

~~ Path 3 — mdoc API docs: ref/ over lib/, on Mono/Linux ~~

mdoc was fed the lib/ implementation assemblies, which still carry ABI-compat
members marked [Obsolete(error: true)] (e.g. by-value SetMatrix(SKMatrix)).
mdoc's comparer ignores the by-ref marker and sorts unstably, and because it
runs in merge mode the pair swapped places every run — a 2-cycle with no fixed
point. The C# compiler strips error-obsolete members from ref/, so docs.cake
now prefers the ref/ surface (lib/ fallback) and invokes mdoc via Mono so the
path runs on Linux.

~~ One home, one set of entry points ~~

The API-diff and release-notes engines moved out of the release-notes skill and
scripts/infra/shared into scripts/infra/docs alongside docs.cake (git renames).
local / CI / Docker now all call the same git-free shell entry points
(generate-{api-diffs,release-notes,api-docs}.sh), and a reproducible Linux
image (scripts/infra/docs/docker) matches CI exactly.

~~ CI, terminology, and docs ~~

A new workflow_dispatch source_branch input (default: main, every existing
trigger byte-identical) lets a manual run validate a feature branch's doc-gen
pipeline before merge, mirroring the docs repo's skiasharp_branch input. The
"changelog" vocabulary — which collided with "release notes" and GitHub's own
"Full Changelog" compare links — is unified onto "API diff" across scripts,
Cake identifiers, log paths, the dev spec, and the recompiled workflow lock;
GitHub's literal compare links are intentionally left as-is. The developer
docs that describe the system are also added/restructured for readability — a
new docs-overview.md map and a re-laid-out release-notes-and-api-diffs.md spec
(both gain a TOC); the relayout is information-preserving and keeps the spec's
numbered headings byte-identical, since ~120 code comments reference them.

~~ Baseline ~~

The regenerated releases/ tree replaces the drifted #4184 output; a full
regeneration in the Linux Docker harness reproduced the committed API-diff
baseline byte-for-byte. The 4.148.0/ and harfbuzzsharp/14.2.0/ API-diff trees
are deliberately left deleted to prove CI's post-merge self-heal recreates
exactly them (the PR description records the expected 33-file recreate set).

4195.title: [v4] Promote remaining pre-v4 obsoletes to error and trim obsolete enums from the ref assembly
4195.body:
[v4] Promote remaining pre-v4 obsoletes to error and trim obsolete enums from the ref assembly (#4195)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3681
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3682

Completes the v4 deprecation pass. The SKPaint text/font subset was already
promoted to error in #3732; this finishes the remaining pre-v4 warning-only
obsoletes now that every one of them has a stable replacement:

  * GRBackendRenderTarget(int, int, int sampleCount, GRVkImageInfo) and the
    GRMtlTextureInfo overload (iOS/macOS/tvOS) -> the ctors without sampleCount
  * SKRunBuffer.GetGlyphSpan(), SKHorizontalRunBuffer/SKPositionedRunBuffer.
    GetPositionSpan(), SKRotationScaleRunBuffer.GetRotationScaleSpan()/
    SetRotationScale() -> the Glyphs / Positions properties
  * the SKPaintHinting and SKFilterQuality enums -> SKFontHinting / SKSamplingOptions

As part of the same pass we audited the bumped Skia milestone range for APIs
deprecated or removed upstream (#3682) and found no SkiaSharp wrappers that
needed new [Obsolete] warnings for this release, so none were added.

~~ Strip the now-unused enums from the reference assembly ~~

With SKPaintHinting and SKFilterQuality marked error-obsolete, every remaining
consumer is itself error-obsolete, so the enums no longer belong in the public
v4 surface. They are removed from the reference assembly (gone from IntelliSense
and uncompilable against) while staying in the implementation assembly for ABI.

The earlier approach removed the enum *types by name* via an inline Cecil
MSBuild task. That was non-deterministic — it would silently strip any future
non-obsolete consumer — and it crashed Cecil on write because the upstream
RemoveObsoleteSymbols task left orphaned get_/set_ accessor methods behind (the
C# compiler does not copy a property's [Obsolete] onto its accessors), which
also kept the enums looking "used." This replaces that workaround with
Mono.ApiTools.MSBuildTasks 0.6.0, whose RemoveObsoleteSymbols now also removes
the compiler-generated accessor methods and backing fields
(https://github.com/mattleibow/Mono.ApiTools.MSBuildTasks/pull/24). The trim is
now attribute-driven: the removal closure follows from [Obsolete(error: true)]
itself rather than a type-name match. Restore pulls 0.6.0 from the dotnet-public
mirror; no nuget.config change ships.

~~ Keep two DrawText overloads at warning ~~

SKCanvas.DrawText(text, ..., SKFont, SKPaint) (the two overloads without an
explicit SKTextAlign) are corrected from error back to warning. They were not
obsolete in the last shipped stable (v3.119.x) — they were marked error during
v4 development, skipping the deprecation-warning cycle. Per the deprecate-then-
error policy a newly-deprecated API must first ship as a warning, so they ship
as a warning in v4 and can be promoted to error in a later release.

SKMetalView (Apple) is updated to call the GRBackendRenderTarget ctor without
sampleCount, since the sampleCount overload is now an error.

4196.title: Make API-diff changelog generation host-independent
4196.body:
Make API-diff changelog generation host-independent (#4196)

The API-changelog comparer produced non-deterministic output. When a
referenced assembly fails to resolve, Mono.ApiTools.NuGetDiff silently
degrades type matching and dumps the affected types as spurious "New Type"
entries. Which references resolved depended on what happened to be installed
on the build host, so the same packages regenerated 111 files on Linux CI but
only 93 on macOS — and the larger diff tripped the gh-aw safe-outputs cap
(E003: more than 100 files in a pull request), blocking the update-release-notes
auto-run from ever landing a clean changelog PR.

Make the diff a pure function of its input assemblies by resolving every
reference with a real, pinned dependency. CreateNuGetDiffAsync now adds each
dependency explicitly via AddDep (a package's lib/<tfm>) or AddPackageDir (an
arbitrary package subfolder), pinned in scripts/VERSIONS.txt — the framework
reference packs, the GTK/GIR and MAUI stacks, SkiaSharp's own inter-package
references, and the Xamarin.Forms platform renderers (the iOS/macOS renderers
ship under build/XCODE11 rather than lib/, so they need AddPackageDir).

The sole assembly that ships in no package — _Microsoft.Android.Resource.Designer,
generated into every .NET-Android assembly by AndroidUseDesignerAssembly — is
skipped with IgnoreResolutionErrors = true. It is unresolvable identically on
every host and is never public API, so skipping it is deterministic and cannot
reintroduce host-dependent churn. Any future unexplained "New Type" churn means
a dependency is missing and must be added as a real AddDep/AddPackageDir, never
ignored.

~~ Regenerated changelogs ~~

With resolution now deterministic, regenerate the changelog tree: new changelogs
for 4.147.0, 4.148.0 and 4.150.0, plus HarfBuzzSharp 8.3.1.6 and 14.2.0. Five
historical diffs are corrected where references now resolve fully — the full
GTK/Gtk.DrawingArea interface chains, and the spurious "Added interface ISKGLView"
dropped from SkiaSharp.Views.Maui.Controls (ISKGLView is a Maui.Core type,
correctly recorded only in the Core changelog; the broken cross-assembly
reference had been misreported as a Controls interface addition).

~~ CI self-heal check ~~

This change also deletes documentation/docfx/releases/4.150.0/ on purpose. The
update-release-notes auto-run regenerates the changelog trees on every push to
main/release/**, so dropping one release here lets the post-merge auto-run prove
it detects the gap and regenerates 4.150.0 (opening a follow-up PR only because
there is a non-empty diff). A full Linux regeneration confirmed the design is
deterministic: all existing changelogs reproduced byte-identically and the
deleted 4.150.0 regenerated to the exact 23 files removed here.

The resolution design is documented in
documentation/dev/release-notes-and-changelogs.md (§5.2 "Deterministic
resolution" + behavioral invariant 9).

4197.title: Fix docs.cake moniker collision dropping iOS GL API docs
4197.body:
The docs-update-frameworks task stages every TFM folder of a package
family into a single moniker directory with a blind CopyFiles. When two
TFMs ship an assembly with the same file name but a different API surface
(SkiaSharp.Views.iOS.dll exists for both net*-ios, which includes
SKGLView/SKGLLayer/SKPaintGLSurfaceEventArgs, and net*-maccatalyst, which
excludes them via #if !__MACCATALYST__) the last copy wins. The
alpha-last MacCatalyst build clobbered the richer iOS build, so mdoc
documented the GL-less assembly and its --delete pass removed the real GL
type docs.

Stage assemblies per-file instead, keeping the build with the most types
on a name collision so no platform's API surface is lost. Type counts are
read with Mono.Cecil (already loaded via api-diff-tools.cake).

4192.title: docs: latest-only, local-only frameworks docs generator
4192.body:
docs: latest-only, local-only frameworks docs generator (#4192)

Reworks the mdoc "frameworks" API-docs generator (scripts/infra/docs/docs.cake)
into a latest-only, local-only model and cleans up the stale state mdoc
accumulates over time. As SkiaSharp moves to a monthly, multi-line release
cadence, carrying a doc moniker per version (or per major) is unmaintainable
and overwhelms the docs site, so versioned doc sets are dropped in favour of a
single latest-only set per package.

Follows #4184, which extracted the api-diff/release-notes engine out of
docs.cake; what remained here is the mdoc/XML frameworks pipeline, now
simplified.

~~ Generation (docs-update-frameworks) ~~

  * Document each package straight from its extracted output/nugets/ content
    no NuGet version queries or downloads. Run docs-download-output first to
    populate output/nugets/; a missing package fails with a clear
    "run docs-download-output first" message.
  * Emit one plain moniker per package, no version suffix (skiasharp,
    harfbuzzsharp, skiasharp-views, skiasharp-views-maui, skiasharp-harfbuzz,
    skiasharp-vulkan, skiasharp-direct3d, skiasharp-skottie,
    skiasharp-scenegraph, skiasharp-resources). All per-version/per-major
    grouping, the preview "stable frontier" rule, the DOCS_MINIMUM_VERSION
    floor, and the HarfBuzzSharp special-case are removed.
  * Keep the NuGetDiff comparer solely to supply mdoc's --lib search paths;
    mdoc still needs third-party reference assemblies (Microsoft.iOS/macOS/
    MacCatalyst/tvOS, Maui, GTK, WindowsAppSDK) to resolve external types used
    by SkiaSharp.Views.*.

~~ Formatting / cleanup (docs-format-docs) ~~

mdoc only ever adds state and never removes it, so dropped or renamed packages
leave stale entries behind. The formatter now keeps the tree in lockstep with
what was actually built this run:

  * collapse <AssemblyVersion> history to latest-only
  * drop stale index.xml <Assembly> overview and emptied <Namespace> entries
  * delete orphan ns-*.xml stubs (always preserving the global ns-.xml)
  * strip stale <AssemblyInfo> blocks from types/members, dropping members and
    deleting type files left empty
  * remove two dead type-specific hacks (the SKDocument.CreatePdf and SK3dView
    [Obsolete] strips) that no longer match the current build; keep the generic
    framework-token safety nets

The net effect on removed APIs: a removed package/assembly (Forms, UWP,
watchOS) drops out entirely; a removed type whose assembly still ships
(e.g. GRBackendRenderTargetDesc) is deleted; a removed member of a surviving
type is the only residue mdoc can leave behind (one across the whole tree), and
once removed the pipeline does not re-add it.

Verified against the latest build output: 10 plain monikers with FrameworksIndex
in lockstep, 0 FrameworkAlternate/FrameworkOnly tokens, index.xml down to 22
assemblies with 0 empty namespaces, ns-.xml preserved, 0 <AssemblyInfo> blocks
with more than one <AssemblyVersion>, and a re-run on its own output (including
the merged docs main) is a zero-change no-op.

Scope is strictly the frameworks/mdoc docs/ pipeline; the release-notes/api-diff
engine is untouched and build.cake still forwards docs-api-diff* to the
release-notes skill. The regenerated docs ship separately via
mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs, so this PR carries no docs submodule bump. The only
other file touched is a one-line comment fix in .agents/skills/api-docs/SKILL.md.

4193.title: [infra] Run release-notes Prepare in its own disk-managed job
4193.body:
[infra] Run release-notes Prepare in its own disk-managed job (#4193)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/27767832525
Fixes: #4191

The first post-merge auto-run of the unified release-notes + API-changelog
workflow (#4184) failed with `No space left on device` ~11.5 minutes in, opened
no regeneration PR, and auto-filed failure issue #4191. The deterministic Prepare
phase (`generate.sh` -> Cake `docs-api-diff-past` + Python `--all`) ran as
pre-agent host steps *inside* the agent job, sharing its disk and clock. The
historical API diff downloads every published package of both the SkiaSharp and
HarfBuzz families (prereleases included); after the HarfBuzz peer family roughly
doubled the download set, Mono.ApiTools.NuGetDiff's package cache exhausted the
~14 GB hosted-runner disk and took the whole job down. The failure was also
invisible until the job died, because the script hid all Cake/Python progress in
a temp log to keep stdout clean for the "Files to polish" list.

Move Prepare into a dedicated `prepare` job so the heavy, network-bound
generation can neither starve nor hide from the agent. The job gets its own
runner, a 120-minute timeout, and a free-disk-space step that drops unused
preinstalled toolchains before the NuGet diff. It runs the generators verbose, so
all progress (and any disk/timeout failure) is visible in the job log. It then
hands its result to the agent as a workflow artifact: a binary git patch of every
working-tree change (the releases tree, the co-release-map sidecar, the author
cache, any pruning) plus the files-to-polish list. The agent job declares
`needs: prepare` (added automatically by the gh-aw compiler), resets to a clean
origin/main, replays the patch with `git apply --3way`, and polishes prose only --
it no longer runs cake/python/git-write itself, and python3 is dropped from its
tool allow-list.

While here, settle the polish-list handoff on one simple contract. The Python
engine now ALWAYS writes the "Files to polish" list to a file -- a plain list,
one repo-relative path per line, no decoration -- defaulting to the gitignored
output/files-to-polish.txt; an empty file still means "nothing changed", which is
what suppresses the no-op PR. There is no stdout-scraping path and no "====" /
"Files to polish:" summary block anymore: everything (progress and the raw list)
streams to STDERR, and the list lives only in the file. The automated workflow
restores that list to the very same output/files-to-polish.txt the agent reads,
so the skill's Polish phase is byte-for-byte identical whether it was triggered by
the workflow or run by hand. The release-notes SKILL.md was trimmed to match: it
no longer describes jobs, runners, artifacts, or /tmp paths -- only "manual = run
the script then read output/files-to-polish.txt, automated = skip the script and
read the same file".

  * generate-release-notes.py: write_polish_list() always writes the file (and
    echoes the raw paths to STDERR); --polish-list overrides only the location;
    the decorated stdout summary blocks are gone.
  * generate.sh: run verbose (no temp-log redirect); forward --polish-list.
  * update-release-notes.md/.lock.yml: define jobs.prepare with disk management +
    artifact upload; the agent restores the list to output/files-to-polish.txt.
  * SKILL.md: drop the workflow plumbing; always point at output/files-to-polish.txt.
  * release-notes-and-changelogs.md (the spec) updated first: standalone job,
    verbose output, always-a-file polish list, artifact handoff, plus a new §7.2
    invariant so this cannot silently regress.

A workflow_dispatch smoke test on the branch (run 27773439793) confirmed the job
graph fires -- pre_activation -> activation -> prepare, with the free-disk and
clean-main steps passing. The scripts themselves only run for real once merged,
because both jobs reset their tree to origin/main before generating; a failed
post-merge run auto-files an issue, so a regression stays visible.

4184.title: [docs] Unify API-diff + release-notes into one agentic workflow
4184.body:
[docs] Unify API-diff + release-notes into one agentic workflow (#4184)

The API changelogs and the website release notes were two disconnected
systems. Each had its own version-comparison logic and lived in a different
place (changelogs/ vs documentation/docfx/releases/), driven by a separate
workflow. They drifted: a line could get release notes but no matching API
diff, or be diffed against the wrong baseline, because the Cake side and the
Python side each guessed at "what is the previous version" independently.

The 4.147/4.148 cycle made the cost concrete. 4.147 shipped preview-only and
never went stable, and the old auto-detection handled that supersession case
inconsistently across the two engines. Fixing it once, shared, was the
trigger for this change.

This unifies both systems onto one versioning model, one engine pair, and one
workflow that opens a single PR, with all output living in the in-site
documentation/docfx/releases/ tree so changelogs and notes stay consistent.

Versioning model:
  * scripts/infra/docs/versions.json is now the single source of truth for
    both engines. It is override-only and family-bucketed (skiasharp /
    harfbuzzsharp): the default baseline for a line is the previous emitted
    line, and an entry is added only to declare a non-default compare_to or
    to mark a line superseded. The old per-engine auto-detection is gone.
  * Superseded preview lines still emit pages: 4.147 and 4.148 both diff
    against the last stable 3.119.4.

HarfBuzzSharp peer family:
  * HarfBuzzSharp versions independently of SkiaSharp, so it now has its own
    hub pages and API-diff folders, linked to the SkiaSharp line it ships
    with via a generated co-release map, and grouped by major.minor.x in the
    TOC. Both engines and the spec treat it as a first-class peer rather than
    a special case.

Workflow and layout:
  * A deterministic Prepare host step (full SDK + network) runs Cake API-diff
    then Python release-notes and emits a clean "files to polish" list; the AI
    Polish step rewrites prose only, copying script-owned content verbatim. A
    no-op run produces no PR.
  * The API-changelog engine was extracted out of docs.cake into the skill's
    api-diff.cake plus shared helpers; docs.cake now owns only the mdoc/XML
    framework-docs pipeline, which was verified to still run end to end.
  * The standalone api-diff.yml workflow and the top-level changelogs/ tree
    are removed; CI callers point at the in-site releases/ tree.
  * documentation/dev/release-notes-and-changelogs.md is the durable spec for
    the versioning model, orchestration, on-disk layout, both engines, and
    editing rules.

This PR also deletes the newest generated lines (SkiaSharp 4.147.0/4.148.0/
4.150.0 and their HarfBuzz peers 14.2.0 and 8.3.1.6) on purpose, so the
post-merge scheduled workflow regenerates them and opens its own PR — an
end-to-end dogfood of the automation.

4188.title: [security-audit] Add Chromium release heads-up to the security-audit skill
4188.body:
[security-audit] Add Chromium release heads-up to the security-audit skill (#4188)

Context: https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule

The security-audit skill could enumerate outstanding Skia CVEs but gave no
early warning when SkiaSharp's `main` falls behind the Chrome Beta milestone —
so the team could miss the window to land a Skia bump before a security fix
reaches stable users.

SkiaSharp's `main` tracks the Chrome Beta milestone. As a milestone graduates
Beta -> Stable -> Extended stable, a `release/<major>.<M>.x` branch is cut from
a `main` already on that milestone, so on the milestone axis those release
lines are inherently covered. The single signal that matters is:

    main_milestone >= beta_channel_milestone

The new tool makes that gap visible and shows how much lead time remains
before the next milestone reaches the stable channel. It is scheduling
context, not a security check on its own, and pairs with the existing Chrome
Releases and Skia CVE resolution steps to set urgency.

The implementation was deliberately simplified. An early per-channel tracker
and a `--check-backports` flag were removed: the within-milestone backport
question requires comparing a mono/skia fork SHA against an upstream
google/skia SHA, which are not comparable. That analysis already lives in
skia-cve-resolution.md. The flag surface was trimmed from 9 to 4 (`--ahead`,
`--window`, `--json`, `--output`), and `PLATFORM` is fixed to "Windows", the
only platform that carries all five channels.

A GPT-5.5 + Opus 4.7 review caught a silent-failure: when the Beta lookup
fails, the original code returned `status="current"` — a false green that hid
the loss of the only signal that matters. The fixes:

  - missing Beta -> status="unknown" + a loud alert, never false-green
  - `critical` now keys off the live Stable/Extended channel milestone rather
    than only the scheduled stable date

ChromeOS, and Android; Chromium-based products like Microsoft Edge;
applications like LibreOffice (Skia is the default, now mandatory, GPU

4179.title: release-notes: restore in-flight -unreleased naming + per-preview rollup (R1/R2/R3)
4179.body:
release-notes: restore in-flight -unreleased naming + per-preview rollup (R1/R2/R3) (#4179)

The versions.json supersession migration (#4171/#4174) correctly made
"which version supersedes which" deterministic via versions.json, but its
move from per-push branch runs to a bulk `--all` pass silently regressed
three documented behaviours. #4174 migrated the pages without the script
emitting the data those pages used to contain, so the features were dropped
on the next regeneration instead of failing loudly.

Three regressions, each restored from a deterministic source (not heuristics):

R1 — in-flight naming. 4.148 and 4.150 were written as terminal
`{version}.md` and the cleanup pass then deleted the real
`{version}-unreleased.md`. Root cause: `--all` picks the rc.1/preview.1
branch as canonical for the version. Fixed with a terminal-vs-in-flight
rule in `_page_filename` (a suffix-less `release/X.Y.Z` branch exists, or
`status: superseded` in versions.json => `{version}.md`; otherwise
`{version}-unreleased.md`) plus an ownership filter in `cmd_all` so the
line head (main / `release/X.Y.x`) owns the `-unreleased` page and the
matching rc/preview branch is deferred instead of colliding.

R2 — in-flight `.x` rollup was a servicing delta instead of the full
cumulative rollup. `determine_diff_range` now honors the versions.json
`compare_to` first (4.148.0 -> 3.119.4) and only does a servicing delta
once the `.0` has actually shipped a stable tag.

R3 — the trailing `## Preview N (date)` sections were lost. The original
3.119.2.md (#3763) and TEMPLATE.md have them and SKILL rules 9/10 mandate
them, but #4174 deleted them on regen because the script never emitted
preview data. `collect_preview_milestones` now enumerates them from the
published prerelease git tags within the page's diff range (deduped to the
latest build per milestone, dated, with chained compare links). A page
rolls up a skipped predecessor minor's previews too, so the 4.148 page
lists the 4.147 previews that match its rolled-up PRs.

Two separate deterministic sources, no magic: versions.json answers "which
version supersedes which"; published tags answer "which previews shipped
and when". Documented in code comments (R1/R2/R3) and a new SKILL.md
"Page naming & preview rollup" section so this can't silently regress on
the next migration. Validated with an offline `--all` dry-run: correct
`-unreleased` filenames, 4.148 rolls up 4.147 p1/p2/p3 + rc1, no bare
4.148.0.md/4.150.0.md, 3.119.x unchanged, and the 3.119.2 compare links
reproduce the original page exactly.

4177.title: [docs] Unify changelog + release-notes generation: stable rollups and local skia links
4177.body:
[docs] Unify changelog + release-notes generation: stable rollups and local skia links (#4177)

Context: #4171 (shared versions.json), #4173 (bot/api-diff PR), #4176 (folded in here)

Two fixes to the shared versions.json-driven docs pipeline, shipped together
because they are the two halves of the same "one rollup per release line"
model.

~~ API changelogs: one folder per release line, not per preview ~~

The unify-versioning refactor (#4171) started passing --nugetDiffPrerelease=true
to docs-api-diff-past so the 4.x line — which ships only as previews/rcs until
it stabilises — would get changelogs at all. But the loop still emitted a folder
for *every* enumerated version, so each intermediate preview produced its own
directory: the last API Diff run filled bot/api-diff (#4173) with
4.147.0-preview.{1,2,3}, 4.148.0-rc.1.2 and 4.150.0-preview.1.1 dirs across every
tracked package (~2,300 added files). Historically changelogs/ held stable
versions only.

Collapse the feed to one entry per release line (numeric version core with the
prerelease label stripped: 4.148.0-rc.1.2 -> 4.148.0; a genuine 4-part stable
like 1.49.2.1 keeps its fourth digit) and emit a single rollup changelog per
line, diffed against the line's representative package — the newest stable if it
shipped, otherwise the newest prerelease. This mirrors the release-notes pages,
which are stable-named rollups of the previews in between.

A line is emitted when it shipped stable, or when it is an active dev line
(preview-only, not superseded, and newer than the last stable — e.g. 4.148,
4.150). Abandoned preview-only lines (superseded in versions.json, e.g. 4.147)
and old never-shipped previews are skipped; their changes are absorbed into the
successor's cumulative diff. Baselines are unchanged: versions.json compare_to
overrides win, otherwise diff against the previous emitted line.

  * RunBreakingAndFullDiff (published overload) now takes the changelog folder
    name separately from the diffed package version, since they differ while a
    line is still in preview.

For SkiaSharp this regenerates to the stable set plus the two active lines: it
adds 3.119.4 (the shipped stable, previously missing) and the 4.148.0/4.150.0
rollups, and prunes the superseded preview-only 3.0.0 and 3.119.3 directories
that predated versions.json. Once merged, the API Diff workflow regenerates
#4173 with the collapsed set.

~~ Release notes: drop per-PR effort metric, resolve skia links locally ~~

The --all run was timing out: the now-removed "effort" metric and the
companion-skia-PR link resolution each issued one network fetch per PR (162
serial round-trips).

  * Removed the per-PR effort metric entirely (it never appeared in output).
  * Made skia-link resolution pure-local: detect submodule bumps via
    git rev-parse <commit>:externals/skia against the parent, batch-fetch only
    the bumped SHAs (blobless + shallow) into externals/skia, and read each skia
    commit subject to parse the companion mono/skia#N PR — no per-PR network.

Result: companion links resolved for 22/23 skia-bumping PRs in 4.148 (the one
miss is an anomalous backwards gitlink with no PR), and a cold full --all run
drops to ~35s.
